paragraphs: Hyman reports that in Moed Katan 24a, according to the Rif and Dikdukei Soferim [supplied דק״ם], Mar Yochani asked Shmuel. Hyman’s own text reads R’ Yochanan. In Avodah Zarah 16b, Abaye said, “Mar Yehudah told me: In Mar Yochani’s household they worked the mills with wild asses.”

notes.text: שבעי means “who asked,” not a person Shavi’i; בערודי means “with wild asses,” not a place Arudi. The consulted Avodah Zarah paragraph confirms the animals working the mills. The source prints דק״ם, not the usual דק״ס; the intended variants-work reference remains a narrow source question. טחגי and שלגו are contextual spelling irregularities retained in the frozen Hebrew.

Hyman’s our reading refers to his own edition, not the present digital text. The supplied דק״ם is retained; identifying it with DikdukeiSoferim is a tentative contextual proposal, not proof from other OCR patterns. Earlier AvodahZarah16b supports wild asses turning mills, not a place Arudi or millstones, but no new primary paragraph or Rif/apparatus was inspected. שבעי means who asked rather than a person Shavii. The uninspected Yochanan title remains R'.

The photographed notice reads דק״ס, the abbreviation for Dikdukei Soferim. In the apparatus to Moed Katan 24a, Rabbinovicz reports Mar Yochani in a Rif manuscript and in the Venice and Constantinople prints. The consulted Vilna Rif (11b:4) and the Davidson Talmud read Rabbi Yochanan. The Yaavetz records Mar Yochani as a variant, and Shibbolei HaLeket names him as Shmuel’s questioner. The older Rif witnesses are cited here through Rabbinovicz.
